title: the Sri Yantra
hook: a pinch of red powder, and the worship starts at the edge
tomorrow: one short word written at the top of the page. what is it?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Sri Yantra's center: the bindu, where the Goddess is said to sit, and two loving answers about who walks all the way in. Today, the walk itself.
screen: `A WHOLE HOUSE GATHERED TO ONE POINT.`

segments.voice: The smell of a ghee lamp, just lit. A small brass plate: red kumkum powder, a few marigolds, a bell. A grandmother settles cross-legged on the floor, takes a pinch of kumkum between thumb and finger, and reaches out, her lips already moving, a name under her breath. Not to the center, where the Goddess is said to sit. To the outer edge, the square with its gates. The center will have to wait, and nobody in the room seems in a hurry.
screen: `A LAMP, A PLATE, RED POWDER.` → `SHE REACHES FOR THE EDGE.` → `THE CENTER CAN WAIT.`

segments.voice: In Sri Vidya, the layers of these past days each have a name: avarana, an enclosure, a covering. Worship of the yantra walks them in order. It starts at the square, moves through the circles and the lotuses, into the triangles, and only at the end arrives at the bindu. At each enclosure, the worshipper honors the goddesses said to dwell there, as attendants and guardians of that layer. One way to feel it: a guest at a palace isn't marched straight to the queen. There's courtyard after courtyard, a greeting at each, until the last door opens. The worship is shaped like the drawing, and the drawing is shaped like an arrival. A simpler worship lives alongside it in some homes: a pinch of kumkum offered to the yantra for each name in the Lalita Sahasranama. One name, one pinch, the red slowly gathering. Same direction of heart, a different path through it. Here the senses do the teaching. Red powder between the fingers, the smell of the lamp, the sound of names said one after another: the body learns the order before the mind can explain it. Edge first. Center last. Nothing skipped on the way.
screen: `AVARANA: EACH ENCLOSURE, IN ORDER.` · `A GUEST CROSSES EVERY COURTYARD.` · `ONE NAME, ONE PINCH OF KUMKUM.` · `THE BODY LEARNS THE ORDER.` · then, large: `EDGE FIRST. CENTER LAST.`

segments.voice: Stand up, if you can, and walk slowly once around the edge of the room you're in, pausing at each corner for one breath, as if greeting someone there. Then come to the middle of the room, sit or stand still, and stay. If walking isn't possible, trace the edge of your seat with one hand, corner by corner, then rest the hand in your lap.
The Sri Yantra in worship: its avaranas, the enclosures, honored one by one from the edge to the center.
Keep this: the Sri Yantra, edge first and center last, the way a guest arrives. Day sixteen thirty-five.

screen: `DAY 1635 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: ONE WORD AT THE TOP OF THE PAGE?`
